active.title: Drop In at the Ocean Bowl Skate Park
active.description: Open since 1976, Ocean Bowl is the oldest continuously operating municipal skatepark in the country — concrete bowls, a street course, and locals who've skated it for three generations.
active.bonus: No skateboard? Rent or borrow one and commit to dropping into the shallow end of the bowl once.

active.title: Pickleball at Northside Park
active.description: The bayside courts at Northside Park fill fast on summer mornings — show up, put your paddle in the rotation, and you'll be playing within twenty minutes.
active.bonus: Win a game against players you've never met — no sandbagging your skill level.

active.title: Kayak Tour Through the Back Bay Marshes
active.description: The guided kayak tours through the Assateague marsh channels get you into the osprey nests and heron rookeries that the bay-side tourists don't know exist behind the hotels.
active.bonus: Paddle silently through the marsh channel until a great blue heron lets you get within 10 feet.

active.title: Boardwalk 10-Mile Morning Run
active.description: The OC boardwalk runs 10 miles from the inlet to 146th Street — run it at 6am before anyone sets up and you have the whole plank, the ocean on your left, the sun rising.
active.bonus: Run the full 10 miles without stopping — all the way to 146th and back.

active.title: Surfside Beach Volleyball Tournament
active.description: OC runs summer beach volleyball leagues and open tournaments on the sand courts near 9th Street — show up, find a pickup game, play until the sun forces you into the water.
active.bonus: Win three sets in a row against people you've never met before.

active.title: Bike the Coastal Highway End to End
active.description: Rent bikes from any of the dozen boardwalk shops and ride the dedicated lane along Coastal Highway from the inlet to the Delaware line — 17 miles each way, flat, the bay on one side and the ocean on the other.
active.bonus: Ride all the way to the Delaware line and take a photo at the state sign.

active.title: Dawn Surf Fishing from the Beach
active.description: Set up before first light with a surf rod and pyramid sinker — bluefish and striped bass run the OC beach in the early hours. The tackle shops on Coastal Highway will tell you exactly where.
active.bonus: Catch and release everything before 8am, then get Thrasher's.

active.title: Body Surfing the Atlantic Breaks
active.description: No board needed — the OC beach break in summer runs 2-to-3-foot waves that body surf perfectly. Get in the water at 7am when the lifeguards set up and the flags are green.
active.bonus: Catch 20 waves before noon — count them.

active.title: Paddleboard the Assawoman Bay
active.description: The flat bay water is perfect for stand-up paddleboarding — rental shops on every block of the bay side, the OC skyline behind you, herons in the marsh grass ahead.
active.bonus: Paddle to the marsh grass on the far side and look back at the whole city from the bay.

active.title: Volleyball at the 3rd Street Courts
active.description: The permanent sand volleyball courts near the inlet at 3rd Street draw serious pickup players every summer afternoon — jump in and you'll be playing competitively within five minutes.
active.bonus: Challenge the winning team directly and win at least one set.

active.title: Run the Assateague Loop Trail
active.description: The Life of the Dunes and Life of the Marsh trails at Assateague Island NPS loop through live maritime forest and tidal marsh — a 3-mile run that feels nothing like a beach vacation.
active.bonus: Run both loops back-to-back before 7 AM and finish before the first tourist bus arrives.

active.title: Bike the OC Boardwalk at Dawn
active.description: Rent a cruiser from one of the 2nd Street shops and ride all three miles of the boardwalk before 8 AM — the planks belong to you, a few joggers, and the pelicans.
active.bonus: Ride the full length without stopping — north Inlet to 27th Street and back — no dismounting.

chill.title: Get Lost in The Ocean Gallery
chill.description: The boardwalk's most gloriously chaotic landmark — a collaged building stuffed floor-to-ceiling with thousands of paintings, prints, and oddities that has defied curation since the 1960s.
chill.bonus: Buy the single weirdest piece under $20 you can find — display it at home without explanation.

chill.title: Afternoon Hammock at Assateague State Park Campground
chill.description: String a hammock between two loblolly pines at the Assateague State Park campground and let the salt breeze and cicadas do the rest.
chill.bonus: Fall asleep in the hammock — actually asleep, not just eyes closed.

chill.title: Afternoon at Northside Park Bayside Lawn
chill.description: Northside Park's wide bayside lawn is where OC locals actually go — bring a blanket, watch the herons work the shallows, and let the afternoon disappear.
chill.bonus: Spend the whole visit without looking at your phone — leave it in your bag face-down.

chill.title: Miniature Golf — Pirate's Cove at Night
chill.description: The multilevel pirate-themed mini golf course by the inlet at night — waterfalls, animatronic pirates, neon, and a crowd of eight-year-olds who will beat you by six strokes.
chill.bonus: Play both courses back-to-back without keeping score.

chill.title: Boardwalk Morning Before the Crowds
chill.description: The OC boardwalk at 7am is a different city — joggers, sweeping crews, pelicans on the railing, and every shop still shuttered. The 10-mile plank belongs to you.
chill.bonus: Walk the full length, north to south, before any shops open.

chill.title: Kite Flying at 9th Street Beach
chill.description: The beach wind on 9th Street is predictable and strong — buy a kite at one of the boardwalk shops, go to the beach at 4pm, and do something you haven't done since you were 10.
chill.bonus: Fly it until you can't see it anymore — full spool of string.

chill.title: Assateague Island Barrier Beach Walk
chill.description: The national seashore's undeveloped beach stretches 37 miles with no boardwalk, no hotels, and no noise — walk south until the civilization behind you disappears.
chill.bonus: Walk until you can no longer see any buildings in either direction, then stop and sit.

chill.title: Sunrise on an Empty OC Beach
chill.description: Get to the beach before 6am — the sand is raked, the water is still, the pelicans are fishing in the surf, and there is not a single umbrella or chair anywhere.
chill.bonus: Swim before anyone else sets up — the ocean is yours.

chill.title: Assateague Wild Ponies at Dawn
chill.description: Drive 8 miles south to Assateague Island before 8am — the wild ponies walk the beach at dawn, the barrier island is completely empty, and you forget Ocean City exists.
chill.bonus: Don't feed the horses — they're wild, they bite, and rangers will fine you.

chill.title: Sunset Fishing from the Inlet Pier
chill.description: The public pier at the inlet is free to fish from — croaker, spot, and bluefish in season, and even if nothing bites the water traffic and the sunset over the bay are worth it.
chill.bonus: Keep the first fish you catch and cook it for dinner.

chill.title: Read the Afternoon Away at 27th Street Beach
chill.description: The stretch around 27th Street hits the sweet spot — far enough from the Inlet crowds, close enough to boardwalk ice cream — and the beach chairs face straight into the Atlantic.
chill.bonus: Go fully into the ocean at least once — no dipping-your-toes-in halfway measures.

chill.title: Sunset from the OC Inlet Jetty
chill.description: The granite jetty at the southern tip of the island frames the inlet and bay in gold every evening — locals come here instead of the beach for a reason.
chill.bonus: Climb out to the farthest dry rock on the jetty and watch the sun drop below the bay side.

adventure.title: Ride the Antique Carousel at Trimper's
adventure.description: Trimper's has anchored the inlet end of the boardwalk since 1893, and its hand-carved carousel — spinning since the nineteen-teens — is one of the oldest still operating in America.
adventure.bonus: Pick your carousel animal like it matters — then ride the Tidal Wave right after.

adventure.title: Slick Track Karts at Baja Amusements
adventure.description: West OC's sprawling go-kart complex runs a half-dozen different tracks — the slick track rewards controlled slides, and the family grudge races settle themselves.
adventure.bonus: Call your fastest lap before the race — then beat it.

adventure.title: Dolphin Watch on the OC Princess
adventure.description: The OC Princess has run nature cruises out of the West OC harbor for decades — bottlenose pods work the coastline most summer evenings, and the captain knows where they feed.
adventure.bonus: Spot the first dorsal fin before the captain calls it.

adventure.title: OC Rocket Speedboat Run
adventure.description: The bright yellow speedboat out of Talbot Street pier has been throwing spray at fifty miles an hour along the OC coastline for decades — dolphins on a good day, soaked either way.
adventure.bonus: Sit in the front row — the splash zone is the only honest seat.

adventure.title: Tandem Jump at Skydive OC
adventure.description: Skydive OC drops you from 10,000 feet over the barrier island — the whole coastline from Assateague to Delaware unrolls beneath you before the canopy opens and it goes silent.
adventure.bonus: Keep your eyes open on exit — the first three seconds are the whole point.

adventure.title: Crabbing off the Route 50 Bridge Catwalk
adventure.description: The catwalks flanking the Route 50 bridge are a legitimate local tradition — drop a chicken neck line and pull up blue crabs all afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Catch, measure, and release a legal-size jimmy crab by hand — no gloves.

adventure.title: Surf Lesson at 9th Street Breaks
adventure.description: OC has real surf — the breaks at 9th and 27th Street get 2-to-4-foot waves in summer. Hollow Earth Surf Shop runs beginner lessons on the sand before you paddle out.
adventure.bonus: Stand up on at least three waves before you call it a session.

adventure.title: Assateague Off-Road Beach Drive
adventure.description: The Assateague Island off-road vehicle zone lets you drive your 4WD on the actual beach — deflate your tires to 15 PSI, get a permit at the ranger station, and drive until the island thins to nothing.
adventure.bonus: Drive to the farthest accessible point and set up a beach camp — no one else will be there.

adventure.title: Jet Ski the Back Bay — Assawoman Bay
adventure.description: Rent a jet ski from the bay-side marinas and run the Assawoman Bay — the flat water is perfect, the views of the OC skyline and Assateague are the whole pitch.
adventure.bonus: Go full throttle on one straight stretch of open water — at least once.

adventure.title: Deep-Sea Fishing on the Morning Star
adventure.description: The Morning Star headboat out of the Ocean City Fishing Center has run all-day offshore trips since the 1970s — mahi, tuna, and sea bass are real possibilities.
adventure.bonus: Ask the mate to let you reel in someone else's fish when they're gassed — then tip him for it.

adventure.title: Kayak the Assawoman Bay at Assateague Explorer
adventure.description: Paddle the glassy back-bay channels behind the island at sunrise before the jet skis wake everything up.
adventure.bonus: Kill the paddle and sit in complete silence for 60 seconds mid-bay.

adventure.title: Parasailing with Odyssea Watersports
adventure.description: Odyssea launches you 400 feet above the Atlantic from the Inlet, giving you a view of the whole barrier island that no boardwalk postcard can match.
adventure.bonus: Let go of the harness handles for a full 10 seconds at peak altitude.

social.title: Beach Bonfire on Assateague
social.description: Ocean City bans beach fires — Assateague doesn't. Build one below the high-tide line on the National Seashore, and the night runs on driftwood smoke, stars, and whatever the ponies think of you.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to a group you don't know and stay with them for at least one hour.

social.title: Skee-Ball Tournament at Marty's Playland on the Boardwalk
social.description: Marty's Playland has occupied the same boardwalk block since 1943 — the skee-ball lanes are original, the lighting is dim, and winning still feels genuinely good.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to a best-of-three match and actually follow through.

social.title: Fish Tales Bay-Side Deck
social.description: The bay-side bar with live music, tiki torches, and the kind of outdoor deck that was designed for the exact mood you're in at 4pm on a summer Saturday in Ocean City.
social.bonus: Stay for two sets of live music without checking your phone once.

social.title: Brass Rail Bar — OC's Old-School Dive
social.description: The downtown OC dive bar that predates the resort boom — cheap drinks, dark interior on a bright day, and regulars who've been holding these same seats since the '80s.
social.bonus: Ask the oldest-looking regular at the bar when they first started coming here.

social.title: Seacrets Tiki Bar Floating Docks
social.description: The Jamaica-themed waterpark-meets-bar on the bay has floating docks, swim-up bars, reggae all day, and a crowd that's been working toward this specific Saturday since January.
social.bonus: Get in the water at least once before leaving — from the dock, not the pool.

social.title: Inlet Park Boardwalk End Hangout
social.description: The south end of the boardwalk at the inlet — where the fishing boats come in, the carnival rides run until midnight, and the whole town seems to end up by 9pm on a Saturday.
social.bonus: Ride one carnival ride, eat one piece of boardwalk food, talk to one stranger.

social.title: Jolly Roger Amusement Park Night
social.description: The OC amusement park at the end of the boardwalk at night — the Ferris wheel view of the lit-up boardwalk and the ocean is worth the ticket price for that alone.
social.bonus: Ride the Ferris wheel twice — once facing the ocean, once facing the bay.

social.title: Greene Turtle Sports Bar — Game Day
social.description: The OC sports bar that got so popular it became a chain — the original location still has the right energy for a Sunday football game with something fried in your hand.
social.bonus: Pick a game you have no rooting interest in and commit to one team for the full game.

social.title: Fager's Island Sunset Bell — 1812 Overture
social.description: Every night at sunset Fager's plays the 1812 Overture as the sun drops into the bay and the crowd rings the bell together — it sounds ridiculous until you're there doing it.
social.bonus: Ring the bell. Don't be the one person who thinks they're above ringing the bell.

social.title: Classic Car Cruising Week on Coastal Highway
social.description: Every September, tens of thousands of vintage cars take over Coastal Highway for Cruisin' OC — the sidewalks become a rolling museum and everyone is suddenly a car person.
social.bonus: Strike up a real conversation with a car owner and get them to tell you the full story of how they restored it.

social.title: Late Night at the Purple Moose Saloon
social.description: The Purple Moose on the boardwalk is the loudest, most honest bar in Ocean City — live rock and roll nightly since 1985, no VIP section, no pretense.
social.bonus: Request a song from the band between sets and don't let them talk you out of it.

social.title: Live Music Night at Shenanigan's Irish Pub
social.description: Shenanigan's on the boardwalk at 4th Street has hosted live bands every summer weekend for thirty years — the kind of bar where strangers actually talk to each other.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the two people nearest you before the second set starts.

foodie.title: Evening at Galaxy 66 Bar & Grille
foodie.description: Galaxy 66 packs creative cocktails and a raw bar into a converted space on 66th Street that feels nothing like the rest of the OC restaurant strip.
foodie.bonus: Let the bartender build you a cocktail completely off-menu — just name your base spirit and walk away.

foodie.title: Crab Cakes at Waterman's Seafood Co.
foodie.description: This West OC institution on Route 50 has been serving Eastern Shore tradition since 1982 — broiled crab cakes upstairs, a fresh seafood market downstairs, and zero boardwalk pretense.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the table next to you is visibly enjoying — no menu consultation allowed.

foodie.title: Kohr Brothers Frozen Custard Boardwalk
foodie.description: The boardwalk frozen custard stand that's been running since the 1920s — denser and richer than soft serve, in a cone, eaten while walking the boards in the evening crowd.
foodie.bonus: Get the concrete — custard blended with mix-ins — not the cone.

foodie.title: Longboard Cafe Breakfast in North OC
foodie.description: The casual North OC breakfast spot with surfer-bar energy and a full eggs-and-griddle menu — go before 9am to get a table, stay for the surfboard decor and easy-morning feeling.
foodie.bonus: Order the biggest breakfast on the menu and eat every bit of it.

foodie.title: Captain's Galley Crab Cake
foodie.description: The serious crab cake restaurant off the boardwalk — broiled, jumbo lump, almost no filler, served with a side of old-school diner formality that's been here longer than most of OC.
foodie.bonus: Order it without asking what's in it — just let it arrive.

foodie.title: The Shark on the Harbor Waterfront
foodie.description: The waterfront seafood restaurant on the ocean side with views of the inlet — the fish sandwich is the move, eaten at an outdoor table as the fishing boats come in.
foodie.bonus: Ask the server what came in on the boats this morning and order that.

foodie.title: Dumsers Dairyland Soft Serve
foodie.description: The OC soft serve institution since 1939 — the twist cone is the move, eaten on the walk back to the beach before it melts in whatever heat July has decided on today.
foodie.bonus: Order the twist before deciding what flavor you want — the decision is automatic.

foodie.title: Hooper's Crab House Pile-It-High
foodie.description: The OC crab house that doesn't pretend to be anything other than a crab house — steamed blue crabs by the dozen, corn on the cob, and a pitcher of whatever's cold.
foodie.bonus: Order more than you think you need — you always do.

foodie.title: Thrasher's Fries with Old Bay — No Ketchup
foodie.description: The boardwalk fries that have a rule: apple cider vinegar and Old Bay only, ketchup refused at the counter. The line wraps around the stand. The wait is worth it. This is OC.
foodie.bonus: Eat them standing up, on the boardwalk, before they cool down.

foodie.title: Bahia Marina Blue Crab Feast on the Bay
foodie.description: The bay-side crab house with a marina view and newspaper-covered picnic tables — steamed crabs, mallets, Old Bay, and the Assawoman Bay turning orange behind you at sunset.
foodie.bonus: Pick crabs until your hands smell like Old Bay and you can't remember what you were worrying about.

foodie.title: Fractured Prune Custom Donuts
foodie.description: Hot donuts glazed and topped to order at the OC original — pick your glaze and toppings from a board of combinations that makes no sense until you eat one.
foodie.bonus: Order the OC Sandy — the local combination the regulars get without looking at the board.

foodie.title: Steamed Crabs at Crab Alley
foodie.description: Crab Alley in West Ocean City has been slinging Old Bay-crusted steamed crabs on brown paper since 1985 — the kind of messy, mallet-pounding meal that defines the Chesapeake summer.
foodie.bonus: Order a dozen large males and finish every one — no crab left behind.
